subject.statement: Wirecard was audited by EY, which signed off its 2019 accounts.

summary: The claim is mixed: EY was Wirecard's appointed external auditor for 2019, but it refused to sign off the 2019 accounts on 18 June 2020 and therefore did not issue an audit opinion. Thus the subject was audited by EY, but EY did not sign off the accounts.

findings.statement: EY was appointed external auditor of Wirecard for the fiscal year ending 2019.
On 18 June 2020, EY formally refused to sign off Wirecard's 2019 accounts.
EY did not issue an unqualified audit opinion on Wirecard's 2019 financial statements.
EY did not issue any audit opinion (including qualified) for Wirecard's 2019 accounts after the refusal.
After the refusal, EY did not issue a revised opinion or withdrawal; it stated it was seeking clarification.

conflicts: What is the full legal name and jurisdiction of the audit firm referred to as EY? - supported by finance.yahoo.com, wirecard.com (weight 1.05) vs refuted by europarl.europa.eu (weight 0.95)
Did EY later issue any revised opinion or withdrawal after the refusal? - supported by cnbc.com (weight 0.85) vs refuted by europarl.europa.eu (weight 0.95)
conflict_notes: Q2: The full legal name and jurisdiction of EY. Supporting sources (finance.yahoo.com, wirecard.com) indicate EY is Ernst & Young GmbH Wirtschaftsprüfungsgesellschaft, Germany. Refuting source (europarl.europa.eu) focuses on EY's refusal to sign the audit report and does not directly dispute the name/jurisdiction. Weighted more heavily toward the supporting sources, so we accept the German GmbH description.

Q7: Whether EY issued a revised opinion or withdrawal after refusing to sign Wirecard's 2019 accounts. Supporting source (cnbc.com) states EY did not issue a revised opinion and was seeking clarification. Refuting source (europarl.europa.eu) states EY declared fraud and false confirmations, which could be read as a statement but not an audit opinion. Weigh the cnbc.com source as more specific to audit opinion, thus lean toward no revised opinion, but acknowledge residual uncertainty.
